latest_evidence.probe: NATS JetStream Nats-Msg-Id duplicate suppression plus PubAck/double-ack contract comparison
latest_evidence.documented_contract: JetStream PubAck confirms stream storage; Nats-Msg-Id suppresses a repeated stream write only within the stream duplicate-tracking window; a confirmed/double ack confirms that the consumer acknowledgment reached the server.
latest_evidence.scope: Documentation-only comparison of one open-source transport primitive. No NATS server was started, no hosted compute or authenticated service was used, and no external semantic data was read or written.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: A stable Nats-Msg-Id can couple a retry identity to the externally visible JetStream append within the configured dedupe window, reducing duplicate transport writes. However, storage acknowledgment and consumer processing are explicitly separate, and a double ack confirms only the broker acknowledgment. Therefore the documented contract does not atomically couple an arbitrary non-transactional consumer side effect with message consumption; the r255 repository-state CAS baseline remains necessary and the arbitrary-side-effect atomicity gap remains open.
